meta.description: Real-time credit card authorization decision: The program checks incoming authorization requests from an MQ queue and decides whether a card transaction is approved or declined.
meta.process_description: The program reads authorization requests from an IBM MQ input queue (up to 500 messages per run), containing transaction data such as card number, amount, merchant information, and transaction type. For each request, card master data, account information, and customer data are retrieved from the respective files and the IMS database to make the authorization decision. The decision (approval or rejection) is based on business rules such as available credit limit, card status, account status, and fraud indicators. The result is written back as an authorization response to an MQ reply queue.

files.ACCTDAT: Account master file – contains account details including credit limit and available balance
files.CUSTDAT: Customer master file – contains customer master data for the cardholder
files.CARDDAT: Card master file – contains card data including card status and expiration date
files.CARDAIX: Alternative access path to card data via account number (Alternate Index)
files.CCXREF: Cross-reference file – links card number to customer ID and account ID

business_rules: A transaction is rejected if the transaction amount exceeds the account's available credit limit (INSUFFICIENT-FUND)
A transaction is rejected if the card used is not active (CARD-NOT-ACTIVE)
A transaction is rejected if the associated account is closed (ACCOUNT-CLOSED)
A transaction is rejected if the card is flagged as suspected fraud (CARD-FRAUD)
A transaction is rejected if the merchant is classified as suspected fraud (MERCHANT-FRAUD)
A maximum of 500 authorization requests are processed per program invocation to avoid resource overload
After each processed authorization request, a CICS SYNCPOINT is issued to ensure data consistency
The card number is linked to customer and account data via the cross-reference file (CCXREF) before the authorization decision is made
Authorization requests are read from the MQ queue in CSV format and contain date, time, card number, amount, merchant data, and transaction ID

Performs the orderly termination of the authorization process: closes MQ queues, releases occupied resources, and saves the final processing status.
Returns control to the CICS runtime system, thereby terminating the real-time authorization transaction normally without scheduling a subsequent call.
End point of program COPAUA0C after complete processing of all incoming authorization requests from the MQ queue.
Terminates program execution normally after all authorization decisions have been made, responses written back, and syncpoints set.

paragraphs.name: MAIN-PARA
paragraphs.description: MAIN-PARA is the central control paragraph of the authorization program and orchestrates the complete processing cycle: initialization, processing of all incoming authorization requests, and orderly program termination.

paragraphs.name: 1000-INITIALIZE
paragraphs.description: Initializes the authorization process: the program receives the MQ queue information from the CICS trigger, opens the input queue, and reads the first incoming authorization request.

paragraphs.name: 1000-EXIT
paragraphs.description: This paragraph serves as the formal end point of the main processing block '1000'. It marks the end of the top-level control logic before processing of the MQ input queue begins.

paragraphs.name: 1100-OPEN-REQUEST-QUEUE
paragraphs.description: Opens the MQ input queue from which incoming credit card authorization requests are read. Without successful access to the queue, no authorization process can be started.

paragraphs.name: 1100-EXIT
paragraphs.description: This paragraph marks the formal end of processing section 1100 and serves as a structural endpoint within the authorization flow. It transitions to the next processing phase – preparation of the IMS database connection (PSB scheduling).

paragraphs.name: 1200-SCHEDULE-PSB
paragraphs.description: This paragraph establishes the connection to the IMS database by scheduling the required Program Specification Block (PSB) for access to authorization summary data. Without this initialization, no customer data required for the authorization decision can be retrieved from the IMS database.

paragraphs.name: 1200-EXIT
paragraphs.description: This paragraph marks the formal end point of processing section 1200 and serves as a structured return point after completion of the associated processing logic in the authorization process.

paragraphs.name: 2000-MAIN-PROCESS
paragraphs.description: This paragraph controls the central processing loop for incoming authorization requests: it reads, evaluates, and responds to up to 500 credit card transactions from the MQ input queue and ensures data consistency after each decision.

paragraphs.name: 2000-EXIT
paragraphs.description: This paragraph serves as the formal end point of processing block 2000 and marks the end of the main processing loop for authorization requests. It contains no independent business logic but ensures the structural return from the processing block.

paragraphs.name: 2100-EXTRACT-REQUEST-MSG
paragraphs.description: This paragraph parses the incoming authorization request from the MQ queue and extracts all relevant transaction data (card number, amount, merchant information, etc.) from the CSV format to make it available for the subsequent authorization decision.

paragraphs.name: 2100-EXIT
paragraphs.description: This paragraph serves as the formal end point of the associated processing section in the authorization process. It marks the end of the control structure and returns program control to the calling section.

paragraphs.name: 3100-READ-REQUEST-MQ
paragraphs.description: Reads the next incoming authorization request from the MQ input queue and extracts the correlation ID and reply queue to ensure that the authorization decision can later be matched to the original request.

paragraphs.name: 3100-EXIT
paragraphs.description: This paragraph marks the formal end point of the parent processing section and serves as a structural endpoint without any business logic of its own.

paragraphs.name: 5000-PROCESS-AUTH
paragraphs.description: This paragraph controls the complete authorization process for a credit card transaction: it loads all relevant master data, makes the approval decision, and writes the result back.

paragraphs.name: 5000-EXIT
paragraphs.description: This paragraph serves as the formal end point of the parent processing section and signals the end of the authorization processing logic without any further business actions.

paragraphs.name: 5100-READ-XREF-RECORD
paragraphs.description: This paragraph uses the card number to look up the associated customer ID and account ID in the cross-reference file (CCXREF), so that the subsequent authorization check can be directed to the correct cardholder and account.

paragraphs.name: 5100-EXIT
paragraphs.description: This paragraph serves as the formal end point of the associated processing section in the authorization process. It marks the end of the flow control and enables an orderly return to the calling program section.

paragraphs.name: 5200-READ-ACCT-RECORD
paragraphs.description: Loads the account master record of the cardholder using the account ID retrieved from the cross-reference file, in order to provide the credit limit and account balance for the authorization decision. If the account is missing or unreadable, the error is logged and the transaction cannot be approved.

paragraphs.name: 5200-EXIT
paragraphs.description: Formal end point of processing section 5200, which serves as a structural return point within the authorization process and ensures an orderly return to the calling logic.

paragraphs.name: 5300-READ-CUST-RECORD
paragraphs.description: Loads the customer master record of the cardholder using the customer ID retrieved from the cross-reference file, in order to provide the customer data required for the authorization decision. If the record is missing or unreadable, an error is logged.

paragraphs.name: 5300-EXIT
paragraphs.description: This paragraph serves as the formal end point of the associated processing section and enables a structured return to the calling program section in the authorization flow.

paragraphs.name: 5500-READ-AUTH-SUMMRY
paragraphs.description: Retrieves the pending authorization summary from the IMS database for the account associated with the card, so that already reserved amounts can be taken into account during the credit limit check.

paragraphs.name: 5500-EXIT
paragraphs.description: This paragraph serves as the formal end point of the associated processing section in the authorization process. It marks the end of the flow control and enables an orderly return to the calling program section.

paragraphs.name: 5600-READ-PROFILE-DATA
paragraphs.description: This paragraph is intended as a placeholder for loading profile data (card, account, and customer master data) but currently contains no active business logic and is traversed without any processing.

paragraphs.name: 5600-EXIT
paragraphs.description: This paragraph serves as the formal end point (exit label) of the associated processing section in the authorization process. It marks the end of the flow control and enables an orderly exit from the section without any further business logic.

paragraphs.name: 6000-MAKE-DECISION
paragraphs.description: This paragraph makes the final authorization decision for a credit card transaction: it checks the available credit limit, sets approval or decline with a standardized decline reason, and assembles the response message for MQ return.

paragraphs.name: 6000-EXIT
paragraphs.description: This paragraph serves as the formal end point of the authorization processing cycle and enables a structured return from the parent processing block.

paragraphs.name: 7100-SEND-RESPONSE
paragraphs.description: Sends the authorization decision (approval or decline) as a response message to the MQ reply queue so that the requesting channel receives the result of the credit card check.

paragraphs.name: 7100-EXIT
paragraphs.description: This paragraph serves as the formal end point of the associated processing section in the authorization process. It marks the end of the flow control and enables an orderly return to the calling program section.

paragraphs.name: 8000-WRITE-AUTH-TO-DB
paragraphs.description: Persists the result of the authorization decision in the IMS database by first updating the authorization summary and then inserting the new authorization detail record.

paragraphs.name: 8000-EXIT
paragraphs.description: This paragraph serves as the formal end point of the authorization processing block and enables an orderly return to the calling program section after the authorization decision has been completed.

paragraphs.name: 8400-UPDATE-SUMMARY
paragraphs.description: Updates the authorization summary in the IMS database after each authorization decision by incrementing approved and declined transaction amounts and counters.

paragraphs.name: 8400-EXIT
paragraphs.description: Formal end point of paragraph 8400, which serves as a structural endpoint within the authorization processing flow and ensures an orderly return to the calling program section.

paragraphs.name: 8500-INSERT-AUTH
paragraphs.description: This paragraph persists the result of an authorization decision as a detail record in the IMS database in order to archive the transaction in a traceable manner for subsequent reconciliation and fraud checks.

paragraphs.name: 8500-EXIT
paragraphs.description: This paragraph serves as the formal end point (exit label) of the parent processing section and marks the end of the associated business logic without performing any further actions.

paragraphs.name: 9000-TERMINATE
paragraphs.description: This paragraph controls the orderly termination of the authorization program by releasing the IMS database connection and closing the MQ input queue, ensuring that all resources are cleanly shut down.

paragraphs.name: 9000-EXIT
paragraphs.description: This paragraph serves as the formal end point of the authorization program and marks the regular end of the processing logic after all authorization decisions have been completed.

paragraphs.name: 9100-CLOSE-REQUEST-QUEUE
paragraphs.description: Closes the MQ input queue for authorization requests in an orderly manner after all messages have been processed. Errors during closing are logged without interrupting the overall process.

paragraphs.name: 9100-EXIT
paragraphs.description: This paragraph serves as the formal end point of the authorization processing block and enables a structured return to the calling program section after the authorization decision has been completed.

paragraphs.name: 9500-LOG-ERROR
paragraphs.description: This paragraph logs errors that occurred during the authorization process with a timestamp to the central error log. For critical errors, the entire authorization run is immediately aborted to prevent data loss or inconsistencies.

paragraphs.name: 9500-EXIT
paragraphs.description: This paragraph serves as the formal end point (exit label) of a parent processing section in the authorization process. It marks the end of the associated procedure and enables a structured return to the calling program section.

paragraphs.name: 9990-END-ROUTINE
paragraphs.description: This paragraph forms the orderly program termination of the authorization process. It ensures that all open resources (MQ connections, files) are cleanly closed and the CICS transaction is terminated normally.

paragraphs.name: 9990-EXIT
paragraphs.description: This paragraph serves as the formal end point of the authorization program and marks the regular end of the processing logic after all authorization decisions have been completed.
